data.name: Maia
data.gender_notes: Maia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Mother of the God of Wisdom
data.long_meaning: In Roman mythology, Maia was the goddess of motherhood, fertility, and growth. In Christianity, Maia is associated with the Blessed Virgin Mary and symbolizes the mother of God. The name Maia carries the meaning “Mother of the God of Wisdom” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Maia usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of the god of wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the nurturing and protective nature of a mother, and the wisdom of the divine mother.
data.etymology: Maia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of the God of Wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maia total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: מיה
in_hebrew.meaning: מייה - גדולה, אמא, או מי גדול
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מיה מקורו בשפה העברית ומשמעותו 'מייה' או 'גדולה'. הוא קשור למילה העברית 'מים' ויכול להיות קשור גם למילה 'אם', שפירושה 'אמא'. השם מופיע בתנ'ך ככינויה של דמות נשית, אך לא באופן ישיר כשם עצם.

in_greek.name: Μαῖα
in_greek.meaning: Μαῖα - μεγάλη, μητέρα, ή μεγάλη μητέρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μαῖα προέρχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'μεγάλη' ή 'μητέρα'. Στην ελληνική μυθολογία, η Μαῖα ήταν μια από τις Πλειάδες, κόρη του Ατλαντα και μητέρα του Ερμή. Ο όνομα έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί στην Εκκλησία ως ένδειξη σεβασμού και πνευματικής καθαρότητας.

in_latin.name: Maia
in_latin.meaning: Maia - great, mother, or fertile land
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Maia originates from Latin and signifies 'great', 'mother', or 'fertile land'. It was used in ancient Roman culture to denote the earth and fertility. In Christian tradition, Maia is associated with purity and spiritual growth, reflecting its roots in ancient cultures.

in_english.name: Maia
in_english.meaning: Maia - a great, motherly figure, symbolizing fertility and spiritual growth
in_english.long_meaning: The name Maia, originating from Hebrew and Greek roots, signifies 'great' or 'mother'. It is associated with fertility, spiritual growth, and purity. In Christian tradition, Maia represents a figure of maternal love and devotion. The name has been used across cultures, symbolizing a connection to the earth and divine feminine.

data.cultural_impact: Maia holds the heritage of an ancient Roman goddess, who was traditionally viewed as the embodiment of motherhood and fertility. In modern times, this name may invoke images of maternal love and nurturing. It also has Biblical associations. For instance, in the New Testament, during Jesus' ministry, an unnamed woman brought her young son to him for a blessing. This scene has been linked to the traditional significance of Maia, showcasing a loving mother bringing her child close to a guiding figure or spiritual authority.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Maia holds significant spiritual power by connecting the bearer to the Christian symbol of the Blessed Virgin Mary. By invoking this connection, the Maia name encourages nurturing spiritual growth and the fostering of a strong maternal connection to God. It also represents the themes of motherhood and dedication to caring for others, especially loved ones. Ultimately, as a Christian name, Maia is a testament of hope, grace, and unwavering love.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Maia, derived from the Latin word for "Mother of the Gods," symbolizes the nurturing and maternal aspects of the divine. In Christian tradition, it represents the love and care of the Virgin Mary for Jesus and all humanity.

historical_references.reference: In Greek mythology, Maia was a nymph and the mother of Hermes by Zeus. She was also the goddess of spring growth, and was said to have given birth to Hermes while she was tending the cattle of Zeus on Mount Cyllene.

Maia of Arimathea, a woman from the region of Judea, is mentioned in the New Testament as having been present at the crucifixion and burial of Jesus. Tradition holds that she was the foster mother of Jesus during his childhood, and that she provided the linen cloth for Jesus' burial.

modern_usage.modern_context: Maia is a name of Greek origin that means 'mother of the goddess of the earth'. In modern contexts, it's often associated with astrology as it's the name of the second month's celestial body in the Greek zodiac. The name also has ties to mythology, particularly in reference to Maia, a Titaness and mother of Hermes. Lastly, Maia is also seen as a symbol of femininity due to its associations with nurturing and motherhood. On platforms like Instagram, Pinterest, and Tumblr, you can find various representations of Maia, from astrological memes to artwork inspired by Greek mythology.

name_in_real_life.story: Ruth Maia, a minister in Rome, Italy, shares that their name Maia meaning "Mother of the God of Wisdom" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
